publishedWalks.title: The Highgate Village Self-Guided Walk — Richard Jones
stops: Highgate station; Park Walk; North Road Dickens lodging; Highgate School; Gatehouse
Pond Square; Church House; Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute; St Michael’s; Flask
Reservoir; The Grove; Witanhurst; Millfield Lane; Holly Lodge Estate; Holly Village
Cemetery entrances; Waterlow Park; Ivy House; Whittington Stone; Archway station
themes: Two-hour, station-to-station itinerary, not a Highgate-station loop
Dickens, literary associations, village institutions, philanthropy and landscape
stories: Advertises Dickens’s temporary lodging, pub initiation customs, Coleridge’s residence and village water supply. Other passages mix documented associations, fictional settings and attributed anecdotes; these require separation before reuse. Locator: lines 51–200; publication date not stated; commercial guide source family. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village: Tales of History and Mystery — Highgate Society / Deborah Greenfield
themes: Architecture, environment, famous residents, village preservation and folklore
stories: Advertises resistance to road widening in 1962, Waterlow’s public gift, pub horn rituals, Graham Chapman and literary residents. Locator: lines 72–83; page dated August 22, 2025; local society/provider source family. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

The Nell Gwynn window episode is advertised, not independently established here; ghosts and highwaymen must remain attributed folklore rather than documentary fact. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

publishedWalks.title: Highgate Village — a place apart — London Walks
stops: Highgate Underground ticket hall: advertised meeting point
Highgate Cemetery and Kenwood: suggested after-walk visits, not established tour stops
themes: Village lanes, cottages, Georgian houses and London views
stories: Promotional copy names Coleridge, Dickens, Betjeman, Nell Gwyn and numerous modern residents without specifying their individual stopping places. Locator: lines 59–92; publication date unstated; commercial provider source family. No complete itinerary is disclosed. ([walks.com](https://www.walks.com/our-walks/highgate-village-a-place-apart))

publishedWalks.title: Historic walk in Highgate Wood — City of London / Michael Hammerson
stops: Information Hut beside the café: confirmed advertised start
Further numbered stops: unknown because the linked leaflet failed to load
themes: Approximately two-hour self-guided woodland history walk
stories: The landing page identifies the author, duration and numbered-map format but supplies no individual historical stories. Locator: lines 25–31; updated October 29, 2024; municipal publisher source family. This is a partially catalogued guide, not a reconstructed itinerary. candidates.name: Highgate Underground public exterior / Park Walk approach
candidates.why: Proposed orientation and return anchor, not an accepted stop. The Jones guide uses Park Walk on its village approach, offering an alternative to an entirely main-road ascent. Exact station exit, public standing space and current path continuity remain unverified. Locator: lines 51–58. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: North Road Dickens lodging
candidates.why: A possible small-scale story of family finances and temporary accommodation rather than a generic famous-author stop. The guide places the family here in August 1832. Public pavement anchor and exact surviving address must be established; the guide’s relative building description is insufficient. Locator: lines 58–62. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate School exterior
candidates.why: Potential institutional-history contrast to resident biographies: the guide describes foundation, decline and nineteenth-century revival. Proposed anchor is public pavement, never school grounds; precise building identification and primary corroboration are pending. Locator: lines 67–74. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Gatehouse exterior
candidates.why: Could explain the settlement’s name through movement, land ownership and tolls. The guide links the pub name to a former gateway; surviving fabric must not be confused with the historical gate. Proposed pavement viewpoint and safe crossing require verification. Locator: lines 74–77. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Pond Square
candidates.why: A public-space candidate connecting a vanished pond with social customs and the shape of the village. Both surveyed providers use it, so selection should depend on revealing physical detail rather than repetition of familiar folklore. Exact standing point and pond history need corroboration. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Highgate Literary and Scientific Institute, South Grove exterior
candidates.why: A less celebrity-led candidate about local learning and the circulation of knowledge. The guide identifies the institute at No. 11 and dates its foundation to 1839. Anchor would be public pavement; no library admission is assumed. Locator: lines 93–97. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: St Michael’s Church exterior
candidates.why: Potential story of parish boundaries and the relocation of Coleridge’s remains. Exterior narration must distinguish an unseen burial from visible architecture. Use public South Grove frontage unless courtyard access is independently confirmed. Locator: lines 100–104. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: Reservoir mound near The Grove
candidates.why: Infrastructure candidate: the guide associates the reservoir with the New River Company and piped supply in 1854. It could connect an ordinary visible mound to changing daily life. Visibility, public viewpoint and the exact water-supply proposition need verification. Locator: lines 114–118. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: 3 The Grove, Coleridge residence exterior
candidates.why: Possible focused account of a household, medical care and literary conversation. The guide identifies a plaque and residence from 1823 to 1834, but its visitor list is not accepted evidence. Proposed public-road viewpoint must respect residential privacy; addiction requires careful, non-sensational treatment. Locator: lines 122–124. ([london-walking-tours.co.uk](https://www.london-walking-tours.co.uk/free-tours/highgate-village-walk.htm))

candidates.name: High Street / village preservation
candidates.why: A potentially strong collective-action story rather than another individual biography. The Highgate Society describes a 1962 demolition threat associated with road widening and residents’ opposition. Which visible frontage best demonstrates the threatened scheme remains unknown; obtain the plan and contemporary records before narration. Locator: lines 72–73. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

candidates.name: Waterlow Park / Lauderdale House exterior
candidates.why: Landscape and public-benefit candidate: the Society’s walk explicitly connects the park and house and advertises Waterlow’s gift. Select one precise exterior viewpoint rather than treating the whole park as a stop. Gate hours, path gradient, visibility and the return-loop cost are unverified; exclude the advertised Nell Gwynn window anecdote unless properly qualified and corroborated. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))

candidates.name: Highgate Cemetery western entrance from Swain’s Lane
candidates.why: Exterior-only candidate for cemetery architecture and its relationship with the village. The Society uses this entrance as its start. No admission, access inside, grave visibility or personal cemetery experience is assumed. Pavement capacity and additional descent/ascent may make this unsuitable for the hour-long loop. ([highgatesociety.com](https://highgatesociety.com/highgate-village-tales-of-history-and-mystery/))
